rules.when: A non-coding task depends on fresh news, current events, live public facts, or recent market and product changes.
rules.why: Grok is the preferred dispatch when current web-connected context is central to the work. grok has one provider family, so it needs no provider declaration.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: Keep complex code work on the approved default; a higher model requires the captain's explicit per-task decision. The Codex rule floor remains the captain's headroom policy: a known shortfall falls through to default, while a floor naming a provider or scope quota-axi does not report is unverifiable and escalates instead.
